name: STSPIN32F0ATR
title: Three-phase BLDC controller with embedded STM32F031 MCU
summary: STSPIN32F0A is a system-in-package BLDC motor controller: an STM32F031C6 Cortex-M0 MCU (48 MHz, 32 KB Flash, 4 KB SRAM) together with a three-phase gate driver for external N-channel MOSFETs, rated 600 mA sink and source with integrated bootstrap diodes and cross-conduction interlock. It runs from 6.7 to 45 V and makes its own 3.3 V (buck) and 12 V (LDO) rails, and adds three op amps for shunt current sensing and an overcurrent comparator with three thresholds. UVLO on every supply, thermal shutdown and a standby mode are built in.

circuits.title: Application example: three-shunt field-oriented control
circuits.description: The chip runs a three-phase motor through three external half-bridges, each with a shunt in its low-side source, for field-oriented control. The internal buck converter makes the 3.3 V VDD rail from VM through L1 and the freewheel diode D1, and that rail feeds both VDD and VDDA, each with its own decoupling capacitor. CREG holds up the internal 12 V regulator at VREG12. Per phase, HSx and LSx drive the MOSFET gates through gate resistors, and CBOOTx between VBOOTx and OUTx is the bootstrap capacitor. Both ends of each shunt go to the op amp inputs and the overcurrent comparator; the op amp outputs are read by ADC inputs PA0 to PA2, and the comparator sees the current feedback through the RLP/CLP low-pass. PA3 reads the bus voltage from the RBUS1/RBUS2 divider with CBUS, and PA4 reads board temperature from an NTC to VDD with RTH to ground and CTH. PB6/PB7 carry the USART, PA13/PA14 the SWD port, PF0/PF1 Ready and Alarm lines; NRST has CRST and a push-button to ground, BOOT0 a pull-down, and TESTMODE is tied to GND.

circuits.title: 8 MHz crystal on the HSE oscillator
circuits.description: An 8 MHz resonator with built-in load capacitors CL1 and CL2 hangs across PF0 (OSC_IN) and PF1 (OSC_OUT), with REXT in series on the OSC_OUT side. The feedback resistor RF and the gain stage are inside the MCU. REXT depends on the crystal and is set from its manufacturer's data; resonator and capacitors sit as close to the two pins as possible.

circuits.title: Op amp signal conditioning
circuits.description: Each of the three op amps is wired as a difference amplifier: INN reaches OPxN through an input resistor, with a feedback resistor from OPxO back to OPxN; INP reaches OPxP through an input resistor, with a resistor from OPxP to ground. OPxO goes to an ADC input. Shown on op amp 1; op amps 2 and 3 take the same network.

operation.text: A system-in-package that pairs an STM32F031C6 microcontroller (extended-temperature, suffix 7) with an analog IC built in BCD8s (0.18 µm). The analog IC holds a three-phase half-bridge gate driver for external N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs, a 3.3 V buck regulator, a 12 V linear regulator, three rail-to-rail op amps and an overcurrent comparator with a selectable threshold. The MCU suits field-oriented control, six-step sensorless and other BLDC algorithms.

Cortex-M0 core at up to 48 MHz, 4 KB SRAM with hardware parity, 32 KB Flash, CRC unit, up to 16 fast I/Os (5 V tolerant), the advanced-control timer TIM1 for PWM, up to 5 general-purpose timers, a 12-bit ADC with up to 9 channels (single or scan), I2C, USART and SPI, and SWD debug. Operating range -40 to 125 °C.

SRAM runs at CPU clock with zero wait states and raises an exception on a parity error. Option bytes write-protect Flash in 4 KB blocks and set readout protection: level 0 none; level 1 blocks Flash access when a debugger is attached or the part boots from RAM; level 2 also disables SWD and RAM boot. BOOT0 and an option bit choose boot from user Flash, system memory or SRAM. The system-memory bootloader reprograms Flash over the USART on PA14/PA15. Flash is aliased at 0x00000000 and stays reachable at 0x08000000.

VDD feeds the I/Os and the MCU's internal regulator; VDDA feeds the ADC, reset, RC oscillators and PLL, and comes from the internal buck or from an external 3.3 V source. VDDA must be at least VDD and must come up first. Power-on and power-down reset hold the MCU in reset below about 2 V; POR watches VDD only, PDR watches VDD and VDDA (the VDDA monitor can be disabled by an option bit when VDDA ≥ VDD is guaranteed). A software-enabled programmable voltage detector can interrupt when VDD crosses VPVD. MCU low-power modes: sleep (CPU stopped, peripherals running), stop (1.8 V domain clocks stopped, PLL, HSI and HSE off, SRAM and registers kept; woken by an EXTI line, PVD, RTC, I2C1 or USART1) and standby (1.8 V domain off, SRAM and registers lost except RTC domain; woken by NRST, IWDG, a WKUP pin rising edge or an RTC event).
Every unused GPIO inside the package is set by software to output, driven low, after start-up.

VM, VDD, VREG12 and each VBOOTx have their own UVLO. A supply enters undervoltage below its turn-off threshold and leaves it above its turn-on threshold. VM or VDD UVLO switches off the linear regulator, op amps and comparator and holds all six gate outputs low; VREG12 UVLO holds all gate outputs low; a VBOOTx UVLO holds only that phase's high-side output low. In UVLO the outputs are held low by the driver's N-channel device.

With VM rising past VMOn and PWR_OK, the buck brings VDD up over tSS; VREG starts rising once VDD has passed VDDOn. With VM falling, VREG leaves regulation below about 13 V and the linear regulator stops near VMOff, VREG then decaying as its capacitor discharges; the buck stops at PWR_OK and VDD decays the same way.

Temperature sensors sit beside the buck and the linear regulator. An overtemperature turns off the block concerned (buck or linear regulator), which restarts on its own once the temperature drops below TSD - Thys.

The internal buck makes 3.3 V for the MCU and for external loads, works in discontinuous conduction mode and has a fixed soft-start time to limit inrush. A fault on SW that reaches IOVC latches the regulator off; only cycling VM restarts it. A fault on the output that pulls VDDA below VDDOff makes the regulator restart with a fresh soft-start, repeating until the overload clears, with inductor current limited to ISW,peak.

3.3 V can be fed straight into VDDA instead. With SW left open or tied to VM, the internal switch keeps switching on the internal clock; with SW tied to GND or VDD, the switch sees a short and latches off. VDD must never be applied from outside while VM is below VDD.

A 12 V LDO from VM supplies the gate driver section and needs a capacitor on VREG12. It is for the internal circuitry only and must not power external parts. When VM is below 12 V, VM and VREG12 can be tied together so the gate drivers run straight from the supply. With VM rising, VREG12 switches on at VM = 7.5 V and climbs with VM to 12 V at VM = 13 V; with VM falling, it sags below 12 V and switches off at VM = 7.2 V.

Driving OC_TH_STBY1 (PF7) and OC_TH_STBY2 (PF6) both low puts the analog IC in standby after tsleep: the linear regulator turns off, all gate outputs are pulled low, the op amps and comparator are disabled, and the buck keeps running. On leaving standby VREG12 needs a recovery time tREG = CREG × VREG12 / IREG12,lim.

Three half-bridge drivers, 600 mA source and sink, for N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs. Each high side runs from a bootstrap supply charged through an integrated bootstrap diode. Every driver input has a 60 kΩ typ pull-down so outputs stay low during start-up and whenever the MCU is not driving them. An interlock keeps the high- and low-side outputs of one half-bridge from being high together.
TIM1 acts as a three-phase PWM on six channels with complementary outputs and programmable dead time; TIM1_CH1 to CH3 drive HS1 to HS3 and TIM1_CH1N to CH3N drive LS1 to LS3.

The high-speed external clock comes from an external clock signal or from a 4 to 32 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator on PF0/PF1. An external clock must meet the I/O characteristics: high and low levels VHSEH and VHSEL, rise and fall times tr(HSE) and tf(HSE) measured 10 % to 90 %, high and low times tw(HSEH) and tw(HSEL), period THSE.
TESTMODE enters a test mode; it is shorted to GND in an application so the mode cannot be entered by accident.

Three rail-to-rail op amps with uncommitted inputs and outputs, meant for signal conditioning such as shunt current sensing; their outputs can go to ADC inputs. The output stage recovers quickly from saturation, which occurs when a large input drives the output past what it can swing.

OC_COMP connects to the shunt to watch load current; PF6 and PF7 set the internal threshold to 100, 250 or 500 mV. On a trip the comparator signals PB12 (TIM1_BKIN) and PA12 (TIM1_ETR). With OC_SEL (PA11) high it also acts on the gate driver logic directly, turning off all three high-side outputs and so the external high-side switches; with OC_SEL low (default) only the MCU sees it.

A comparator input pulse shorter than tOCdeglitch is ignored; a longer one reaches PB12 and sets the latched OC signal (OC_blk_n) tCPD after the input crosses. Once the overcurrent has gone, the latch is released at the first high-side input rising edge after all three high-side inputs (HS1 to HS3) have stayed low for more than tOCrelease.

Digital and analog I/Os are protected by diodes to the 3.3 V VDD rail and to GND. The VM, VREG and high-side driver (VBOOT to OUT) domains have active ESD clamps. The OUTx, HSx, LSx and SW pins are built to go below GND.

The application example uses three shunts and field-oriented control, with VDD (3.3 V) from the internal buck, VREG12 (12 V) from the internal LDO, USART on PB6/PB7, SWD on PA13/PA14, Ready and Alarm lines on PF0/PF1, a dedicated reset, overcurrent protection by the internal comparator, current sensing with the internal op amps and ADC (PA0, PA1, PA2), bus voltage compensation via PA3 and temperature monitoring via PA4.
Custom VFQFPN48 7 x 7 mm with a reduced exposed pad, connected to ground inside, that leaves room for vias beneath the package. Lead finish Ni/Pd/Au.
